name: pacman
description: The package manager of Arch Linux and its derivatives: fast, simple, and combined with the Arch User Repository via AUR helpers.

flags.description: Full system sync + upgrade — the Arch update ritual.
Install a package (combine: -Syu PKG installs and updates in one go).
Remove / remove with unneeded deps and configs.
Info / file list of an installed package.
List orphaned packages (installed as deps, no longer required).
Find which package provides a file (needs -Fy first).

examples.explanation: Synchronizes the package database and upgrades everything. On Arch, do this regularly — partial upgrades are unsupported.
Installs htop from the official repositories.
Lists orphans; sudo pacman -Rns $(pacman -Qdtq) removes them all.
Builds the file database, then finds which package provides lsblk.

about: pacman uses a single flat repository model with rolling releases. The AUR (Arch User Repository) is a community collection of build recipes used through helpers like yay or paru — those packages are compiled from source and are not officially supported.
useCases: Daily package management on Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS.
mistakes: Running pacman -Sy PKG without u (partial upgrade) — Arch explicitly does not support it and it breaks systems.
Installing random AUR helpers/packages without reading the PKGBUILD.
distroNotes: Arch Linux, Manjaro, EndeavourOS, and derivatives only.
